Hi Claire / Tom —

Following our call yesterday, attached is a compact mutual action plan (MAP_v2.xlsx) and a draft test-case pack (eval-testcases.pdf) that map acceptance signals back to concrete verification steps. High-level asks:

- Review the acceptance signal categories on tab "Signals" (quality, latency, availability, security).
- Confirm the specific customer success metrics you want us to prioritize (e.g., exact intent-match vs. top-3 recall).
- Sign off on the proposed go/no-go date (we've penciled in 2026-09-24, see timeline).

Important notes in the MAP:
- Exit gates are explicit (production SLA target, pass rate on 500 validation prompts, audit log completeness).
- Contingency: fallback to quantized model variant if tail-latency exceeds target in 2 successive runs.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet, tabbed), eval-testcases.pdf (PDF, draft).

I"m looping in Marissa for the acceptance-test definitions, Ben for SLA/ops gating, and Karthik for model/quantization sink checks.

Proposed next steps: quick pass from you on the signals + sign the MAP so we can schedule the 2-week test sprint.

Thanks —

Thanks Grace — quick read looks good. A few clarifications before we sign:

1) Latency signal: are the targets end-to-end (app -> Redwood -> model inference -> app) or only server-side token latency? We need an SLA that accounts for our UI layer.
2) Data residency: the MAP references logs and audit exports. For our compliance team, which fields are persisted in logs and for how long?
3) Acceptance tests: the doc lists a 90% pass rate on intent-match for the first 500 prompts. Can we scope that to a stratified sample that weights high-priority intents higher?

If you can answer 1–3 (and update the MAP accordingly) we'll aim to sign by next Tue.

Subject: Re: Jumpstart MAP: pilot acceptance signals, eval plan & close timeline

Claire / team —

Quick internal input on the acceptance-test design (see attached eval-testcases.pdf for the full list):

- Sampling: agree on a stratified 500-prompt sample (70% critical intents, 30% exploratory). We can provide the sampling script and seed to ensure reproducibility.
- Quality checks: intent-match (binary), top-3 answer recall, factuality spot checks (~50 items). Pass = >= 90% on weighted score.
- Latency: define server-side p95 < 450ms and end-to-end p95 < 700ms (Redwood + app instrumentation). Tom, please confirm whether Veridian's UI agent adds an expected 150–250ms.
- Security gate: audit logs must contain request-id, truncated prompt hash, and model variant. Retention = 90 days by default (we can negotiate).

Risks: our current quantized variant reduces GPU cost but occasionally increases p95 by ~60ms in cold-cache runs. We recommend a canary (10% traffic) for two days before ramp.

Proposed timeline update (in-MAP):
- 2026-09-06: finalize MAP and sampling list
- 2026-09-07 to 09-20: test sprint (2 weeks)
- 2026-09-21 to 09-23: verification window and executive sign-off
- 2026-09-24: planned cutover (if gates met)

Claire — if you approve the weighted pass criteria and the 90-day retention, we"ll update the MAP and circulate for signature.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Claire —

Quick operational note on the SLA gating we included in the MAP:

- If p95 latency exceeds the agreed threshold in 2 consecutive verification runs, Redwood will automatically fail the gate and trigger the fallback policy. That fallback is: route to the quantized model variant with pre-warmed cache and an increased batching window for 30 minutes while we investigate.
- We can instrument synthetic health checks every 5 minutes and surface them to a shared dashboard (we"ll add read-only view access to your SREs).

Karthik / Marissa, please add the dashboard link and health-check metric names to the MAP.

Ben Carter
